quickAnswer: Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) on Istanbul's Asian side is a compact single-terminal hub dominated by Pegasus Airlines and AJet. The M4 metro links SAW directly to Ayrılık Çeşmesi (Marmaray) and Kadıköy in about 50 minutes, while private cars to Sultanahmet or Beşiktaş vary sharply from 50 minutes at night to over 100 minutes in rush hour.
category: Inner Pages — 20 Airport, Cruise Port & Terminal Arrival Guides

body.text: How does the M4 metro connect SAW directly to Kadıköy and Marmaray?

The underground M4 metro line starts directly beneath the forecourt of Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) and runs 33.5 km across 23 stations to Kadıköy Pier in roughly 52 minutes ([M4 Metro Line overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M4_(Istanbul_Metro))). One stop before Kadıköy, at Ayrılık Çeşmesi, you interchange directly onto the undersea Marmaray commuter rail to reach Sirkeci (Sultanahmet) or Yenikapı on the European side in under 15 minutes.

Because the M4 and Marmaray bypass Bosphorus bridge gridlock completely, rail is often the fastest and most predictable option during weekday rush hours (07:30–10:00 and 16:30–20:30) if you travel with manageable luggage. Trains operate roughly from 06:00 to 00:00 daily; buy or top up an Istanbulkart at the station machines before descending to the platform.
How long is a private car from SAW to Sultanahmet vs Beşiktaş in rush hour?

A private car from Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) to Sultanahmet uses the Eurasia Tunnel (Avrasya Tüneli) under the Bosphorus, taking 45 to 55 minutes off-peak and 75 to 105 minutes in weekday rush hour. Reaching Beşiktaş requires crossing the 15 July Martyrs Bridge or Fatih Sultan Mehmet Bridge, taking 50 to 65 minutes off-peak and frequently 90 to 120 minutes during evening congestion.

body.text: If you are staying on the Asian side (Kadıköy, Bağdat Caddesi, Ataşehir, or Üsküdar) or attending a consultation at an Asian-side clinic coordinated via our [medical tourism advisory](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), landing at SAW saves substantial cross-city driving compared with IST.

Pegasus Airlines and AJet (the low-cost subsidiary of Turkish Airlines) account for the vast majority of domestic and international flights at Sabiha Gökçen (SAW). Both carriers connect SAW extensively across Türkiye—including Antalya, İzmir, Bodrum, Kayseri, Trabzon, and Rize-Artvin—and run high-frequency international routes to London Stansted, Germany, the Netherlands, France, the Balkans, and the Gulf.
Follow this low-cost carrier checklist when flying through SAW:

items: Express Baggage drop: Pegasus offers self-service [Express Baggage](https://www.flypgs.com/en/express-baggage) at Islands D, F, and G in SAW, cutting check-in wait times if you print tags at kiosks.

Strict cabin bag sizing: Under the [Pegasus baggage allowance](https://www.flypgs.com/en/pegasus-baggage-allowance), Light Package fares on international routes include only a 40x30x15 cm (3 kg) underseat item; upgrade online if carrying a trolley.
AJet baggage rules: Review [AJet baggage conditions](https://ajet.com/en/corporate/rules-and-conditions/baggage) before adding sports gear or extra kilos; counter fees are steeper than online rates.
Allow extra security time: SAW has two security checkpoints (terminal entrance and airside), and morning departure banks between 06:00 and 09:00 create brisk queues.

body.text: What lounge and Fast Track options exist at SAW?

Sabiha Gökçen offers three Plaza Premium Lounges—the Plaza Premium Bosphorus Lounge (near Gate 205) and Plaza Premium Marmara Lounge (near Gate 204) in International Departures, plus the Plaza Premium Domestic Lounge—alongside Kepler Club rest pods, all accessible via [Priority Pass](https://www.prioritypass.com/en-GB/lounges/turkey/sabiha-gokcen-international) or paid walk-in entry. For priority security and passport clearance, travellers can book ALLWAYS Fast Track ([SAW Fast Track overview](https://hizligecis.com/en/sabiha-gokcen-fast-track)) or eligible airline add-ons.

Unlike IST's sprawling concourses, SAW's compact footprint means gates are a 5- to 10-minute walk from the lounges, making paid lounge entry or Fast Track particularly worthwhile during summer weekend peaks.

faq.q: Is Sabiha Gökçen Airport (SAW) easier to navigate than Istanbul Airport (IST)?
faq.a: Yes. SAW operates from a single, compact terminal with much shorter walking distances from check-in to boarding gates, though security and passport queues can still build during morning and evening peaks.

faq.q: Does the M4 metro from SAW run 24 hours a day?
faq.a: No. On regular weeknights, the M4 metro operates roughly between 06:00 and 00:00. For arrivals between 00:30 and 05:30, use a pre-booked private transfer, official taxi, or Havabus shuttle.

faq.q: How much extra does the Eurasia Tunnel toll add to a taxi from SAW to Sultanahmet?
faq.a: Passengers pay the official Eurasia Tunnel toll on top of the metered fare. While it adds a modest fee, it routinely saves 30 to 45 minutes compared with crossing the northern bridges.

faq.q: Can I walk directly from the SAW terminal to the M4 metro station?
faq.a: Yes. Exit the arrivals hall, cross the covered pedestrian walkway directly across the roadway, and take the escalators or lifts down into the M4 Sabiha Gökçen station—roughly a 4-minute walk.

faq.q: Should I fly into SAW if my hotel is in Sultanahmet or Beyoğlu?
faq.a: Only if the flight fare or direct schedule is significantly better than IST. Otherwise, IST is geographically closer to European-side neighbourhoods without requiring a Bosphorus crossing.

faq.q: Are there sleeping pods or hotels at Sabiha Gökçen Airport?
faq.a: Yes. Airside passengers in International Departures can book hourly rest units at Kepler Club, while ISG Sabiha Gökçen Airport Hotel sits a short walk outside the terminal landside.
